items.title: The etale locus is compatible with base change under flatness or finite presentation hypotheses
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter morphisms.tex (Morphisms of Schemes)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma states that in a cartesian square of schemes the open set of points where the top morphism is etale is the preimage of the corresponding open set for the bottom morphism, provided either that morphism is flat and locally of finite presentation, or it is locally of finite presentation and the base change morphism is flat. The proof reduces to the unramified locus, which is already known to be compatible with arbitrary base change, and then splits into the two cases: in the first the etale locus equals the unramified locus by flatness plus unramifiedness, and in the second flatness of the relevant morphisms is transported along the square and the composition, so that flatness at the image point follows and the etale-at-a-point criterion concludes.
